findings.note: Canonical's doc comment now contradicts the behaviour this shard's test pins. canonical.go:16 states the canonical form leaves "HTML characters and U+2028/U+2029 left as literal UTF-8", but marshalCanonical escapes both separators (types.go:351-352) and TestCanonicalIsToolchainIndependent asserts the escaped form is what the chain hashes. This is the one contract statement a maintainer would read before touching the encoder, and the new test's own comment explains that reverting to raw separators is what CI caught. The comment should say the separators are escaped.

findings.note: CapText reports truncation when nothing was truncated. For max < 2 it returns ("", true) unconditionally (canonical.go:111-113), so CapText("", 0) claims the empty string was truncated. The new TestCapText guards against spurious truncation only via canonLen(s) <= max, which is never satisfied at max < 2 (the empty string still encodes to 2 bytes), so the wart is invisible to the test and the length assertion at canonical_test.go:137 is explicitly gated on max >= 2. Callers that surface the flag as "detail truncated" would report a truncation that did not happen.

findings.note: Builder.Copy is correct only for from == 2 and silently wrong otherwise. checkProvenance requires Origin.Seq to equal the CHILD event's own Seq (fold.go:432), but Copy renumbers copied events sequentially from 2 (builder.go:172) while setting Origin.Seq to the PARENT's Seq (builder.go:174). Those agree only when from == 2. All six call sites pass 2, so nothing is broken today, but the parameter invites a caller to build a log that fails ERR_AUDIT_INVALID{provenance} for a reason that looks like a product bug rather than a builder misuse. Either drop the parameter or renumber Origin.Seq consistently.

findings.note: Copy has two unguarded assumptions about its parent log. builder.go:154 discards the init decode error, so a parent whose first event is not a decodable init yields a zero-valued child InitData with no signal. builder.go:174 indexes pb.lines[ev.Seq-1], which panics with index out of range unless the parent's Seq values are contiguous from 1 - exactly the shape the Override API exists to violate (WithSeq, documented at builder.go:7-8 as being there "so tests can build invalid logs"). Indexing by the loop position instead of by Seq removes the panic.

findings.note: Builder.Event's transition bookkeeping fails open. Both type assertions (builder.go:80 and builder.go:91) accept only a TransitionData value; a caller passing *TransitionData, a map, or a struct literal of another type gets no iter increment and no state advance, and the resulting log is rejected later by Apply's state/iter check with a message that points at the machine rather than at the test fixture. A t.Fatal-free helper cannot report this, but panicking or requiring a typed AddTransition method would.

findings.note: Builder.stamp takes an Override slice it never uses (builder.go:101, signature parameter `_ []Override`). Init passes o to stamp and then applies the same overrides itself (builder.go:64-68); Event passes nil. The parameter is inert today, but it reads as though stamp applies overrides, and a maintainer wiring it up would double-apply them for Init.
